title: Suppe mit Biskuitschöberl (Soup with Biscuit Shoerl)

steps: Fold 3 egg yolks and a pinch of salt gently into the stiff snow of 3 egg whites

description: A soup made with cauliflower, bouillon, and egg yolks.

ingredients.name: Toasted bread roll slices, fine dumplings, or similar

steps: Blanch well-cleaned cauliflower florets in hot water and then simmer in good bouillon until completely soft. For 6 lothes of cauliflower, take 2 pounds butter and let it sweat in the butter after removing from bouillon. Place in soup pot (terrine). Draw off broth with several egg yolks, season with salt and nutmeg, and pour over cauliflower. May add toasted bread roll slices, fine dumplings, or similar. The soup can be further improved by adding minced chicken or veal breast, crayfish tails and similar, with some crayfish butter added.

title: Suppe mit einem Pudding von mehreren Farben (Soup with a Many-Colored Pudding)
description: A soup made with bread, butter or beef or lard, and egg yolks.

ingredients.name: 1/4 pound butter or good beef lard

steps: Soak a bread roll with crust removed in milk
Beat 1/4 pound butter or good beef lard until fluffy
Add the well-squeezed bread roll
Beat in 6 eggs and 2 egg yolks, one after another
Add finely diced marrow
Make two types of mixture: one red from crab butter and one green from clarified spinach juice
Cut each type into large cubes and add to the mixture
Stir gently in so as not to break apart the cubes
Dust with as much flour as can be held between five fingers
Coat a cloth with butter
Place the mixture on it
Tie tightly with string so it cannot rise
Place in a pot of simmering, slightly salted water
Let it cook for a whole hour
Remove and untie the cloth
Place the pudding in a serving dish
Pour meat broth or consommé over it
Serve at table

Mix salt, pepper, some bread crumbs, and 2 spoonfuls of good cream well together and add to the mixture. Butter a cloth, place the mixture on it, tie together and simmer in boiling salt water for one hour. After removing, place in soup pot and pour brown soup over it.

title: Suppe mit Lungenstrudeln (Soup with Lung Strudel)
description: A soup made with heart, egg yolk, and dough.
steps: Cook a calf's lung with heart until soft
Remove the esophagus and chop the rest finely
Warm a piece of butter
Add finely chopped green parsley and let it warm through
Add the chopped lung with salt and ground pepper
Let it brown a little
Beat 2 whole eggs and 1 egg yolk over it
Stir it well together
Let it cool
Make ordinary strudel dough and stretch it thin
Fill the lung mixture into it, leaving an empty space of about one and a half spans in the middle
Cut the empty space in the middle
Roll the dough from both sides together so the empty space wraps around the filled part several times
Press with a flour-dusted cooking spoon handle one small finger length through
Separate these parts with a knife
Place them in a light brown soup and serve

title: Suppe mit Reis (Soup with Rice)
description: A soup made with rice, meat, and parmesan cheese.

ingredients.name: half a measure good meat soup

steps: Pour half a measure of good meat soup over 4 pounds rice for 6 persons, which should first be washed with cold water, then lukewarm, and finally hot water until nothing white comes off anymore (because it often takes on a stale smell from lying in barrels)
Let it cook salted, without stirring, until tender if you want to serve it with brown soup; you can also stir it often once you have fricasseed it with eggs

Since the poured soup will be drawn into the rice, put it in a dish and pour a measure of beef soup colored with consommé over it, salt it and serve it to the table, and you may also present grated Parmesan cheese on a separate plate

If you do not want the soup this way, stir 3 egg yolks whisked with a spoonful of water into the beef soup to be added until it becomes thick, then serve it with the rice, and sprinkle both this and the brown soup with nutmeg flower

title: Suppe Tortue (Turtle Soup)
description: A soup made with beef broth, celery, and parsnip or parsley root.
steps: Make a good broth and add cleaned celery heads, parsnip or parsley root, yellow turnip roots with some thyme and marjoram.
Fill with broth and cook until the beef sliced 2 inches thick and the veal knuckles are half-cooked.
Take a 2-pound carp, wash it clean, cut it into pieces, and add it to the broth.
When the meat is completely tender, strain the soup through a fine hair sieve and keep it hot.
Make a force from 1 pound of pike and separately from 1/2 pound of veal meat.
Take the yolk from 2 hard-cooked eggs, stir it smooth in a casserole with a proportional piece of butter, add some salt, a little flour, and 1 egg yolk.
From a cooked veal foot, remove all bones and cartilage and cut each piece into fine thin strips, placing them immediately into the soup.
Alternately form small round dumplings with a spoon from the pike force and the veal meat force, and poach these along with the egg yolk force in boiling broth.
Make the soup very hot, season with pepper, and add 1 quarter liter of Burgundy wine.
Let it stand at the fire to become hot again, but do not let it come to a boil; serve when properly warmed in the soup pot.
Drain all the various dumplings in a sieve and add them to the soup.

title: Sweet Rice Croquettes (Süße Reis-Croquettes)

title: Süße Maccaroni (Sweet Macaroons)
description: Prepared with sweet almonds, egg whites, and lemons.
steps: Blanch 1 pound sweet almonds in boiling water, then plunge into cold water for a few minutes
Remove the skins and wash them, then let them dry for 24 hours under a napkin
Take a handful of almonds, pound them in a mortar or on a grater until fine but not too fine so they do not become oily
Pour the white of one egg onto the crushed mass, stir and mix well until it becomes a fine dough
Empty the mortar and proceed with the remaining almonds in the same way, using additional egg whites as needed
Once all the almond mass is processed, return it to the mortar and add 2 pounds of finest pounded sugar and the zest of 2 lemons
Stir all well together and add enough egg white so the dough achieves the necessary consistency

Take a two-finger-wide wooden ruler with a handle, place some dough on it, hold the instrument with your left hand, and use a clean knife to set oblong-round heaps about finger-thick on a sheet of paper, spacing them one and a half inches apart
Push the macaroons on a sheet into a moderately hot oven and bake them slowly for three quarters of an hour
Ensure the almonds are very dry before putting them in the mortar
Be careful when beating the eggs so that no yolk mixes with the white, as this would ruin the entire dough mass and the macaroons would collapse in the oven instead of rising
Keep the oven only moderately heated as almonds and sugar burn very easily
To be completely safe, put a couple into the oven as a test and bake for three quarters of an hour; if they are not burned and have a beautiful yellow color, the oven has the right temperature
If they are black underneath, it shows the lower heat is stronger than the upper, and in this case lay 2 or 3 sheets of paper on the baking sheet to moderate the effect
Only after testing the oven heat in this way should the macaroon dough be placed on paper, and only when completely cooled should the macaroons be removed from it

title: Süßländische Dampfnudeln (Southern-style Steamed Dumplings)
description: Prepared with yeast, melted butter or lard, and melted butter.

ingredients.name: 2 Deka yeast dissolved in 1/4 liter uncooked milk
10 Deka melted butter or 8 Deka lard

steps: Mix together in a deep bowl 60 Deka flour, 4 Deka sugar and 5 grams salt
Dissolve 2 Deka yeast in 1/4 liter uncooked milk with constant stirring and keep it on the warm stove until the milk becomes lukewarm

Beat 4 Stercks butter and 1 whole egg together with 1/8 liter uncooked milk and pour this at the same time with the dissolved yeast into the middle of the flour, stir into a dough and beat finely until it detaches from the spoon
Again stir in 10 Deka melted butter or 8 Deka lard until the dough is combined with the butter
Let the dough rise covered beside the stove in a warm place until it has risen about halfway
In a butter-brushed casserole, pour in enough lukewarm milk to cover the bottom
Using a spoon, place large pieces of the dough next to each other in the casserole, each time brushing them with melted butter
When the casserole is filled, let it stand covered in a warm place until the dough has risen somewhat
Drizzle it once more with melted butter and bake for 3/4 hour in a fairly hot oven
After this time, turn out the casserole, separate the dumplings from one another, arrange them on a platter and serve at table with custard or cream

flesh from a couple of old hens together with their bones

Put the dough on a board dusted with flour and let it rest 1/2 hour in a cold place

title: Tendron de Veau à la Broche (Stuffed Veal Breast Roasted on the Spit)

ingredients.name: ½ teaspoon finely cut green parsley

title: Torte in Naturbutter Wittemaße (Cake in Natural Butter Spanish Style)
description: A cake made with bacon, egg whites, and powdered sugar.

ingredients.name: desired fruit foam or frozen dessert

steps: Cut approximately 8 round discs from white writing paper.
In the middle of each, cut out circular openings so that each disc forms a ring; each successive ring becomes somewhat narrower, with the eighth ring being approximately one finger-width broad.
Line all paper strips with unsalted bacon and place them side by side on a baking sheet with the lined side facing up.
Beat 8 egg whites stiffly and lightly mix with 32 deca vanilla sugar.
Using a paper cornet or syringe, pipe this mixture onto the paper rings without interruption and at even height (approximately finger-high).
Sprinkle with finely pounded sugar.
Additionally, cut a round disc the same size as the broadest ring, brush it with unsalted bacon, and likewise cover it finger-high with the snow mixture and sprinkle with finely pounded sugar.

Dry all of these in the oven at high heat. As these rings take up considerable space on the baking sheet and it is usually not possible to dry them all simultaneously, they can be made in batches, though the snow mixture should always be prepared only shortly before piping and placing in the oven.
Once completely dry, carefully remove the rings from the paper with a sharp, thin knife.

Place the large round disc on a cake plate, arrange the broadest ring on top and secure with egg glaze or white marmalade; arrange all remaining rings, each progressively smaller, as well as the bottom ring on top.
Fill the middle empty space with desired fruit foam or frozen dessert and serve the cake immediately on an appropriate platter.

title: Tourte aux noix (Walnut Cake)

ingredients.name: 24 teaspoons peeled and passed almonds pounded with shell

steps: Mix together 24 teaspoons finely pounded walnuts, 24 teaspoons finely pounded sugar, 24 teaspoons peeled and passed almonds pounded with shell and 1 pinch grated coffee.

Take 6 teaspoons of this mass, place it with 4 teaspoons white bread crumbs in a casserole, pour with 1 1/6 liter boiling water and let it boil for several minutes with constant stirring, then set aside and let cool.
In the meantime, mix the remaining mass, which is placed in a deep pan, gradually with 6 egg yolks and 4 whole eggs, and lastly lightly fold in the snow of 6 egg whites.
Divide this mass into two equal parts, which are filled one by one into cake forms brushed with butter and dusted with flour and baked at low heat for 1 2 hours in the oven.

title: Tremierte Spanferkel (Suckling Pig à la Gelée)
description: Prepared with calf feet, wine, and onion.
steps: Chop the calf feet and pork feet and place them in a braising pan
Add wine vinegar and water and cook together well
Remove the fat and scum carefully during cooking
Add 1 piece of onion pierced with 1 spice clove, 1 yellow turnip, 1 small piece of celery, 5 pieces each of spices, 5 sprigs of parsley, 1 bay leaf, 1 piece of shallot, and some salt
Let everything cook together for one hour
Add the suckling pig cut into desired pieces and cover with white wine
Cook until the meat is sufficiently tender
Remove the meat with a slotted spoon, lay it on a platter and cover with a cloth soaked in white wine
Pour the broth through a sieve and then through a cloth into an earthen vessel and remove the fat carefully
In a braising pan, place the egg yolk from 3 eggs and whisk it slightly with a whisk
Add the suckling pig broth and whisk over the fire until it begins to boil
Pull the braising pan back, cover it with a fitting lid, place it on the same coals
The protein on top will shrink together so that the liquid obtains a clear color
Pour the broth through a cloth as with aspic and set aside in an earthen vessel
Place a mold in ice, pour in strongly finger-deep of the prepared broth and let it cool
Lay the suckling pig pieces with the skin side down on the cooled gelatin so that they join together to form the whole suckling pig
Cover with enough broth to fill the mold

When the liquid is completely cooled, remove the mold, wipe it off, dip it for a moment in hot water, dry it with a cloth, turn it out onto a fitting platter, carefully remove the mold and garnish with the above chopped aspic

title: Trout in Aspic (Forellen mit Aspic)
description: Prepared with aspic and trout.
steps: Choose a small variety of trout that has been boiled blue and cooled in its broth
Chill an oblong smooth mold in ice ½ hour before use
Pour 2 fingers high of very clear, cooled aspic into the mold
When set, arrange the trout so they rest with their backs on the aspic
Position them so the head of one trout lies next to the tail of another
Ensure they do not touch the edge of the mold and appear to swim freely
Use chopped aspic to secure them in place
Add some green parsley between the trout and in their mouths
Carefully pour 2 more fingers high of aspic over them
Break up the remaining trout into unequal pieces
Lay these skin-side down on the set aspic
Fill the mold completely with cooled liquid aspic
Use a tall mold, about twice hand-breadth high
Once the aspic is completely set and covered, remove from ice

steps: Veal carbonades, after the meat has been scraped from the backbone, are beaten flat, sprinkled with salt and pepper, and placed in a shallow casserole with a little very hot butter, to lightly fry them on each side for 1 to 2 minutes so they take on a white color.

A doubly folded paper is cut around as wide as a thumb larger than a cutlet is long, so that when the paper is unfolded it forms a heart shape. When all cutlets are wrapped in this way, they are placed on a sheet of paper soaked in oil or butter which lies on a roasting pan, allowed to fry slowly on both sides, then removed from the paper and arranged in a circle on a serving dish. title: Vol au vent (Puff Pastry Shell)
description: A pastry dish made with butter and eggs.
steps: A chilled butter dough of approximately 1/2 kilogram is rolled out 2 fingers thick and a round plate is cut out.

Butter-brushed paper is placed on a baking sheet, the round dough plate is placed on it, brushed with beaten eggs so far that a strongly knife-back-width margin remains, then the dough is cut with a knife a finger's breadth deep in the rounding so that a 2-finger-wide margin is obtained all around.
The pâté is then placed in the oven and baked at strong heat for 3/4 to 1 hour.
To prevent the pâté from becoming too dark, it is covered with paper once it is yellow.

The pâté, now twice as high, is then removed from the oven, the cut plate is carefully loosened with a knife, removed, and the soft and fatty dough inside is carefully removed with a spoon without injuring the crust at the bottom.
If this is done as quickly as possible, place the pâté in a bowl, fill it shortly before serving with any desired hot ragout, cover it again with the lid, and serve the pâté to the table.

title: Vol au vent Pastries (Small Pâtés) with Filling

From one half of the dough, round pieces are cut out with a pastry cutter, which are placed at finger-width distance on a water-moistened baking sheet, brushed with beaten eggs so far that a strongly knife-back-width margin remains all around, which must never be brushed with eggs so that the dough of the pâté becomes flaky.
From the other half of the rolled-out dough, somewhat smaller pieces are cut out, which are then, to form rings, cut out once more in the middle.
These are now placed on the round plates so that the side which lay on the board does not lie on the brushed plates, but comes to lie upward.
These rings are then brushed in the middle with beaten eggs so far that both outside and inside a knife-back-width margin remains.
They are then placed in the oven and baked yellow at fairly strong heat.
Then remove them with a knife from the sheet, fill the middle empty space with any desired farce, and arrange them elevated in a bowl covered with a napkin.
It is particularly noteworthy that the margin of the pâté must never be brushed or dripped with eggs or water, as in this case the butter dough could not puff up.

description: Prepared with turnips, beef broth, and bread.

ingredients.name: Bratwurst or veal, lamb and pork cutlets

steps: Peel and cut the turnips, let them boil up in hot water, then place them on a strainer, let them drain, put them in a casserole, brown flour in butter, fill with beef broth, and let the turnips cook down with it. Since young turnips are commonly bitter, place a slice of bread in which draws out the bitterness.

Alternatively: place the cut turnips in fresh water, let butter become hot, add the turnips after they have drained, and let them sweat well in it, pour them into a pot, pour boiling meat broth over them, add grated bread or roux and plenty of pepper, and let it simmer until it becomes a thick broth. However, they are better with the bread than with the roux. You can garnish them with bratwurst or cutlets of veal, lamb, and pork.

Or alternatively: when the turnips are peeled and cut, steam them brown in butter, then place one layer in a dish, sprinkle anis and sugar over it, and cover with butter slices; then place another layer of turnips, and so on until all are arranged. Finally pour meat broth over them and let the turnips steam slowly and well covered.

Or alternatively: cut a couple of medium onions into dice, add a fair handful of fresh parsley, steam both with the cut turnips in a fair amount of butter, after an hour add a spoonful of flour, a little caraway, water and salt, gradually pour meat broth over them so they have some but not much broth, stir them frequently, and let them become tender.

title: Zuckerstrudel Brügel (Spit Cake)
description: A cake made with lemon, egg yolks, and butter.
steps: Cream 64 Deka butter until fluffy
Add 64 Deka lemon sugar and 20 egg yolks one after another
Stir in 1 teaspoon nutmeg, an equal amount of blanched spice cloves and cinnamon
Lightly mix in the whites of 15 eggs with 64 Deka flour
Stretch the hollow brügel (a rod that is wide at one end and tapers at the other) onto a spit and secure well with small wooden pegs
When the brügel is warmed through, brush it with paper coated with butter and secure this with twine, which is fastened at both ends of the wood at the ends
Make a bed of charcoal in the base of the spit
Place a long pan under the spit to catch dripping batter
Turn the spit over the fire until the paper is yellow, then drizzle with clarified butter
When it begins to foam, pour the dough mixture with a ladle while rotating the spit evenly until the form is evenly covered
Continue rotating the spit evenly so the batter forms in a point
Let the poured batter turn yellow, then pour the same amount of batter again
Repeat this process until all batter is used
When done, cut the cake evenly at both ends, loosen the twine, remove the spit, carefully remove the cake, place on a plate
After one or two days, sprinkle with various icing, garnish with small sticks and decorate the top with flowers
